{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Michael John Rycroft''' (born 15 July 1938) is an English ionospheric physicist.

==Early life==
{{unreferencedsect|date=October 2026}}
After [[Merchant Taylors' School, Northwood]] (1951–57) his first degree was in physics from [[Imperial College London]] (1960) and his PhD was in meteorological physics from [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]] Cambridge (1964), supervised by Dr T.W. Wormell who had in turn been supervised by Prof [[Charles Thomson Rees Wilson|C.T.R. Wilson]].

==Career==
His research is principally in [[solar-terrestrial physics]] and [[atmospheric electricity]]. In 1977, he was a British finalist in a selection process for European astronauts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spacefacts.de/bios/candidates/english/rycroft_michael.htm|title=Biographies of astronaut and cosmonaut candidates: Rycroft, Michael John|website=Space Facts}}</ref> He began his career at the [[University of Southampton]] (1966-1979) and then moved to the [[British Antarctic Survey]] (1979-1990), where he became director of physical science. Subsequently, he was professor of aerospace at Cranfield University (1990-1994), then at the [[International Space University]] where he remains ''emeritus'' professor. He was a visiting senior research fellow at the Department of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, [[University of Bath]] (2006-2016). He is also a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] and was general secretary of the European Geophysical Society from 1996 to 2003 (part of the [[European Geosciences Union]]).

He has published around 170 papers in the refereed literature,<ref>Web of Science online database, accessed 30 December 2016</ref> edited a significant encyclopedia,<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Cambridge Encyclopedia of Space|others=Rycroft, Michael J.|isbn=978-0521364263|edition=English language|location=Cambridge, England|oclc=22119849|last1=Rycroft|first1=Michael|date=1990|url=https://archive.org/details/cambridgeencyclo0000rycr}}</ref> and co-authored two books on space research.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Whistler and Alfvén Mode Cyclotron Masers in Space by V. Y. Trakhtengerts|last1=Trakhtengerts|first1=V. Y.|last2=Rycroft|first2=M. J.|doi=10.1017/cbo9780511536519|year = 2008|isbn = 9780511536519}}<br />- {{Cite book|title=Spacelab : research in earth orbit|last=David.|first=Shapland|date=1984|publisher=Cambridge University Press|others=Rycroft, Michael J.|isbn=978-0521260770|location=Cambridge [Cambridgeshire]|oclc=11045304|url=https://archive.org/details/spacelabresearch00shap}}</ref> He is currently editor-in-chief of the journal ''Surveys in Geophysics''<ref>''[https://www.springer.com/earth+sciences+and+geography/geophysics/journal/10712 Surveys in Geophysics]''</ref> and was, until 1999, editor-in-chief of ''[[Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics]]''. He edited a Golden Jubilee edition of this journal to commemorate its 50th anniversary in 2000,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rycroft|first=Michael J|date=2000-11-01|title=Preface|journal=Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics|volume=62|issue=17–18|pages=1561|doi=10.1016/S1364-6826(00)00111-5|bibcode=2000JASTP..62.1561R}}</ref> and wrote a highly cited paper on the global atmospheric electric circuit for the same issue.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rycroft|first1=M. J|last2=Israelsson|first2=S|last3=Price|first3=C|date=2000-11-01|title=The global atmospheric electric circuit, solar activity and climate change|journal=Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics|volume=62|issue=17–18|pages=1563–1576|doi=10.1016/S1364-6826(00)00112-7|bibcode=2000JASTP..62.1563R|url=http://www.gt-crust.ru/jour/article/download/59/61}}</ref> On 16 November 2018 a special symposium<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/i/moments/1063836432337436672|title=Prof Michael Rycroft 80th Birthday Symposium|website=Twitter|date=17 November 2018}}</ref> was held in Bath, UK, to mark Rycroft's 80th birthday, with a biographical tribute paper published in May 2020.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Aplin|first1=Karen L.|last2=Harrison|first2=R. Giles|last3=Füllekrug|first3=Martin|last4=Lanchester|first4=Betty|last5=Becker|first5=François|date=29 May 2020|title=A scientific career launched at the start of the space age: Michael Rycroft at 80|url=https://www.hist-geo-space-sci.net/11/105/2020/|journal=History of Geo- and Space Sciences|volume=11|issue=1|pages=105–121|doi=10.5194/hgss-11-105-2020|bibcode=2020HGSS...11..105A|issn=2190-5010|doi-access=free|hdl=1983/e92224c1-b067-4ae7-8e0e-c9245082a976|hdl-access=free}}</ref>
